title.narrative: NCA 2022-2027: Suudu Baaba - inclusive peace in Mopti & Douentza
NORSKA KYRKAN 2022-2027: Suudi Baaba - inkluderande fred i Mopti & Douentza

description.narrative: Insatsen utvecklar fredlig hantering av naturresurser i områdena Djenne och Douentza i kombination med försörjningsskapande åtgärder. Syftet är att minska konfliktnivån i samhället.

The contribution works with peaceful handling of natural resources in Djenne and Douentza in combination with income generating activities. The purpose is to reduce the conflict level in the areas.
The ultimate aim of the project "Suudu Baaba: inclusive peace and socio-economic resiliance in Mopti and Douentza" is to contribute to a community that is more socio-economic resilient and peaceful. The project will be executed for four years, starting October 2022 and is designed around two specific objectives: Specific objective 1: Communities strengthen social cohesion and inclusive natural resource and conflict management mechanisms and structures.Specific objective 2: Communities improve their livelihoods by adapting a more efficient and sustainable use of natural resources in the face of climate change.Norwegian Church Aid (NCA) is lead in a consortium that consists of the international NGO Cordaid and one Malian NGO called Tassaght and a Malian enterprise called Agricap. NCA is responsible for the funds and visavi the Embassy in terms of financial and narrative reporting. Funds will be transferred to other parties.

The consortium has formulated that the overall objective is "to contribute to peace and socioeconomic development in Djenné and Douentza.
Two specific sub-objectives are aligned to this goal. These are: 1. Communities strengthen social cohesion and find peaceful ways of managing natural resources and related conflicts 2. Communities improve their livelihoods by using and adapting a more efficient and sustainable use of natural resources in the face of climate change.

sector.narrative: Civilian peace-building, conflict prevention and resolution

description.narrative:
The Suudu Baaba project went into force in December 2022, for a planned activity period to March 2027. Due to the Swedish governments decision (December 2023) to terminate Swedens bilateral strategy to Mali, the implementation period was shortened to December 31, 2024, and the total project budget was revised from 48 987 368 SEK till 25 000 000 SEK - leaving aproximately 50% of the budget to be implemented in 50% of the project period.
A phase-out plan for 2024 was agreed upon with a reprioritization of activities. The activities that are prioritized during the phasing-out relate to, among other things, water resource management and increasing the livelihood opportunities as well as the food security situation for the population. The expected results relating to these areas were assessed to be largely deliverable, while the overall project objectives were assessed as unlikely to be achieved.
Long-term processes for behavioral and attitude changes, social cohesion and conflict management, were still conducted during phase-out, but given lower priority.
Staff costs and travels for international staff were decreased partly because of the shortened project period, partly because of the security situation that led to less travels for international staff.
The partner Norwegian Church Aid (NCA) has submitted a final narrative report, reporting on indicators of baseline and endline values. Examples of results that were reported:
* Improved access to water infrastructure, increasing coverage from 59% to 77% across 24 villages. Strengthened water management committees through training and support, leading to 56% of community members reporting better service quality and 91% using drinking water services. Additionally, 89% of village committees now integrate climate risk reduction into their planning.
* The project boosted farmer productivity, increasing the proportion of farmers with improved yields from 7% to 52%. This resulted in enhanced access to agricultural inputs and veterinary products.
* 90% of communities could sell products and 87% could access supplies. This success was described to be linked to the project's support for women and youth through training, equipment, and infrastructure for market gardening. Women and youth became more involved in production, processing, and marketing, enhancing their economic empowerment. Participation in national trade events also helped women access better markets. Productivity gains were 57% among male farmers and 46% among women farmers.
* 66% of the climate change monitoring committee members who were involved in trainings to enhance their technical skills adopted climate-adaptive techniques after the trainings. Through these trainings, they adopted adaptation strategies and learned innovative techniques for compost production and land restoration (e.g., assisted natural regeneration, so called half-moon technique as well as solid and liquid compost methods).
* Increase in trust within communities from 39 to 85%, explained by the reduction of mistrust, tensions and violence between groups. Local committees (water point management committees, conflict prevention and management committees, etc) were estalished and members from different communities of religious, ethnic and socio-professional origins consulted each other more regularly, and met to plan and implement joint local development actions of common interest.
* Increase in the percentage of natural resource conflicts resolved non-violently from 28 to 43%. A vast majority of respondents to the end-line study (91%) responded that they are satisfied with the conflict resolution mechanism, with almost equal proportions for women, men and young men.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
